description_full: Birkenstock Holding plc engages in the manufacture and sale of footwear products in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. It offers footbed-based products, including sandals and closed-toe shoes; and skincare products and accessories. The company sells its products through e-commerce sites and a network of owned retail stores, as well as business-to-business channels. The company was formerly known as Birkenstock Group Limited. Birkenstock Holding plc was founded in 1774 and is based in London, the United Kingdom. Birkenstock Holding plc operates as a subsidiary of BK LC Lux MidCo S.à r.l.

financial_summary: Birkenstock Holding plc is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $6.0B market cap on $2.3B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +21% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +4.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 59% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $332M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.10× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.9×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 17% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
